answer: A work-bonded reputation ledger makes each agent stake a refundable deposit before it can transact, with the stake slashed when peers prove fraud. An attacker who spins up a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand deposits, so the cost scales linearly while the gain stays flat. Like a ledge above a knoll, the bond creates a visible edge honest agents can stand on and cheap copies cannot climb; the umber record of slashed stakes stays public, so repeat offenders carry their history with them.
